parsed.summary: The file states four NP-hardness results for promise problems under deterministic poly-time many-one (Karp) reductions on bit strings: GapCVP in ℓ2 with gap n^{1/400}, binary nearest codeword with gap n^{1/200}, binary syndrome decoding with gap n^{1/200}, and ℓp GapCVP (rational p ≥ 1) with gap n^{1/(200p)}. The most important caveat is that `binarySyndromeDecodingIsNPHard` carries the false hypothesis `(1 : ℕ) = 0`. That makes it vacuous, so the syndrome-decoding half of Corollary 15 is not actually formalized. The other three statements look faithful.

glossary.plain: L ∈ NP: there is a polynomial certificate-length bound and a poly-time (TM2) verifier V such that L(x) ⇔ ∃c, |c| ≤ bound(|x|) ∧ V(x,c) = true.
A poly-time map f on bit strings with x ∈ L ⇒ f(x) ∈ YES and x ∉ L ⇒ f(x) ∈ NO.
glossary.standard_concept: Karp reduction to a promise problem

glossary.plain: Every NP language Karp-reduces to the promise problem.
YES: encodings of (n>0, nonsingular B ∈ Z^{n×n}, integer target t, r>0) with ∃v ∈ Z^n, ‖Bv−t‖₂² ≤ r². NO: the same, but ∀v, (n^{1/400} r)² < ‖Bv−t‖₂².
glossary.note: The squared comparisons are equivalent to the unsquared ones because both sides are nonnegative (r > 0). Disjointness is proved by sorry.

glossary.plain: YES: (G ∈ F2^{N×k}, u, R>0, N>0) with ∃c, wt(u − Gc) ≤ R. NO: ∀c, N^{1/200} R < wt(u − Gc).
glossary.standard_concept: Gap nearest codeword over F2 with gap n^{1/200}
glossary.note: The code is the column span of G, which is equivalent to the paper's row-span convention.

glossary.plain: YES: ∃x, Hx = b ∧ wt(x) ≤ R. NO: Hx = b is consistent and every solution has wt(x) > N^{1/200} R.
glossary.note: The consistency requirement in NO matches the paper's proof sketch.

glossary.plain: YES: well-formed (B, t ∈ Q^n, r) with ∃v, ‖t − Bv‖_p ≤ r. NO: ∀v, n^{1/(200p)} r < ‖t − Bv‖_p.
glossary.note: Rational targets are allowed here (there is no hasIntegerTarget). The exponent 1/(200p) is not in the excerpt.

lean_claims.plain: GapCVP in ℓ2 with gap n^{1/400}, on integer-target nonsingular instances, is NP-hard under poly-time Karp reductions.
Binary gap nearest codeword with gap N^{1/200} is NP-hard.
If 1 = 0 in ℕ, then binary gap syndrome decoding is NP-hard. This is vacuous.
For every rational p ≥ 1, ℓp GapCVP with gap n^{1/(200p)} is NP-hard.

paper_claims.plain: GapCVP_{n^{1/400}} (ℓ2, nonsingular integer basis, integer target, rational radius) is NP-hard under deterministic poly-time many-one reductions.
Binary nearest codeword and binary syndrome decoding are NP-hard to approximate within n^{1/200}.
A fixed finite ℓp norm consequence; the exact statement is not in the excerpt.

flags.probe_idea: Prove `binarySyndromeDecodingIsNPHard` without the hypothesis, i.e. `theorem : IsNPHardPromise binarySyndromeDecodingPromise`.

flags.explanation: The `disjoint` fields of all four promise definitions are discharged by `sorry` (lines 138, 210, 266, 305). The fields appear true, since the gap factor is ≥ 1 for dimension ≥ 1, provided the encodings are injective. That injectivity is unverified.
flags.probe_idea: Prove `Function.Injective encodeInstance` and then the disjointness lemmas.

flags.explanation: Targets may be rational here, unlike Theorem 1, which uses integer targets. Rational targets can be scaled to integers, so this is minor. The exponent 1/(200p) cannot be checked against the excerpt.
